enquiry: Our research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface using model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat and liver. We want to compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information, because the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location. This is a laboratory classification study. We need a first comparison experiment and a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

clarification_questions.question: What decision should the classification result support in your research programme, and what would make the current approach insufficient?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the purpose of the comparison and what success looks like.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Decision not stated; the first experiment is treated as a feasibility comparison of the two information sources.

clarification_questions.question: Which tissue classes must be distinguished (for example muscle, fat, liver), and is any specific analyte or fluorescent species of interest?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the classification task and tells whether fluorescence has a defined species to measure.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Classes are tissue types as named; no analyte level is defined, so fluorescence is treated as an unspecified signal until a fluorophore is identified.

clarification_questions.question: What is the physical form of the samples during measurement (fresh, cooked, sliced, homogenised), and are they opaque or translucent?
clarification_questions.why: Determines contact with the ATR crystal, optical depth and whether the surface is representative.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Samples are solid tissue, opaque; surface contact with the ATR tip is assumed to be possible but not verified.

clarification_questions.question: How does the tissue vary within a sample and between samples (texture, fat content, moisture, temperature, time since preparation)?
clarification_questions.why: Heterogeneity and drift affect whether spectra from different spots are comparable and how many replicates are needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Heterogeneity is as stated; variation is unquantified and must be characterised in the lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: Which probe geometry and fiber setup do you plan to use, and can MIR ATR and fluorescence be measured from the same spot, for example with a combi probe?
clarification_questions.why: Same-spot measurement is needed for a valid comparison of heterogeneous samples; fiber type limits MIR transmission.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Setup not defined; the comparison assumes separate probes measuring the same marked location on the sample, which is to be verified.

clarification_questions.question: What is the reference classification of each tissue sample (for example histology, dissection, or a reference chemical assay) and its accuracy?
clarification_questions.why: Without a reference, classification performance cannot be judged.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference method stated; labels are assumed to come from the sample origin (tissue type) and are unverified.

clarification_questions.question: What number of samples, replicates and independent batches are planned, and what accuracy or response time would you consider acceptable for the classification?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the design of a validation on independent runs before any combination of methods is judged.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Sample numbers not stated; the design is a comparison of single methods first, validated on independent batches.

flags_before_revision.detail: different_context: The S04 p.4 study supports IR better for fat and fluorescence better for liver, but the claim says it was on chicken breast, fat and liver; the page mentions these tissues elsewhere (S04 p.3), so this is acceptable. However the claim is about the study finding, which is supported; no clear issue beyond the lab context not being stated as a lab study. Fix: State explicitly that this was a laboratory study on chicken tissue samples, not clinical data.

not_supported: S04 p.4 says IR works better for fat discrimination from PCA, but does not attribute the separation to the ester carbonyl band in the claim's wording; that attribution is on S04 p.3 about the 1740 cm-1 band, and the claim's 'MIR-ATR' label is not stated for the tissue study on the cited page. Fix: Cite S04 p.3 for the ester carbonyl band and say the tissue study used FTIR spectra with ATR probe as reported.

not_supported: The cited pages do not state that ATR probes only a few micrometres in these tissues; the table gives 1-6 um optical depth for ATR probes, but the 'tight contact' requirement is on S01 p.6 only in the DOCX source; the caveat combines several cited items including unrelated rows (cuvette, diffuse reflection) that do not concern ATR. Fix: Limit the caveat to the ATR rows (TABLE:r1, TABLE:r2) and S04 p.2 statement about tight contact with liquid or soft solid samples.

overstated: The claim states the excitation wavelength must suit the tissues as a firm requirement; the sources only describe fluorescence depending on fluorescent species and low selectivity, not a specific excitation-matching rule. Fix: Say that fluorescence depends on the presence of fluorescent components and may need excitation chosen for the sample, as a point to test.

overstated: The page reports the concatenated PCA model revealed three distinct groups for this lab study; the claim presents it as a general finding supporting use for new samples without that scope. Fix: Qualify as a single lab study on three chicken tissue classes with a small sample set (3 samples per tissue type).

not_supported: The cited pages do not provide a fiber-link rule check; S02 p.6 gives transmission ranges but the claim's coverage conclusions (no Vis-NIR coverage for MIR, PIR partial) are derived and S01 p.9 and p.12 do not state them. The S02 chart also lists CIR 1100-6500 nm, which is not addressed. Fix: Report the stated fiber transmission ranges from S02 p.6 and state that the fiber link must be checked against the actual configuration.

not_supported: S04 p.3 says fat spectra are broadened by inhomogeneity; it does not state that freshness and texture can mimic class differences. Fix: Remove the freshness and texture claim or cite a source that states it.

RAMAN.nominal_range: Raman shift in cm-1; signal recorded in the visible / short-wave NIR (400-1100 nm); state the laser excitation separately [S01 p.11]

FLUO.nominal_range: UV/Vis excitation and emission; depends on the fluorescent species [S01 p.12]

UVVIS.nominal_range: UV 190-360 nm and visible; depends on target and setup [S01 p.5]

rule_hints: fluorescence_needs_fluorophore: Fluorescence only measures a defined fluorescent species or a justified indicator; most chemicals do not fluoresce. [S01 p.5; S04 p.4; DOCX §5]
sensitivity_not_selectivity: High sensitivity does not imply selectivity. Fluorimetry and UV/Vis are rated high sensitivity but low selectivity. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); DOCX §5]
nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
combination_is_hypothesis: Combining methods can add complementary information, but the gain is a hypothesis to test against the best single method. [S01 p.7-8; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
